rationale.idea: Run the previously unclosed standalone sequential architecture branch, holding the rest of the recipe conservative, to isolate whether ordered train-history signal has any single-model value on KuaiRand-Pure.
rationale.why_expected_to_help: Validation ranks impressions within user, and train users have much richer histories than the baseline uses; a GRU over chronologically ordered prior long_view items can encode short-term preference drift and repeated motif patterns that a plain FM or order-invariant pooled history cannot. Because the GRU contribution is additive to the FM score, it can help only where sequence carries extra item-specific ordering information, while leaving the robust FM backbone intact.
rationale.grounded_in: Grounded in the menu option description for model=gru4rec_seq, which states that FM/DeepFM/DCN history treatments are set-based while GRU4Rec adds ordered sequence modelling on train-split positives only, citing KuaiRand as 'An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset' (Gao et al., CIKM 2022) and GRU4Rec (Hidasi et al., ICLR 2016). Also grounded in the measured history stats: train users average 43.54 impressions with p90 97, and the hardcoded SEQ_LEN=50 was chosen because it covers p90 of train users; that makes sequence modelling plausible. Finally, the dead-end about ensembling gru4rec_seq with FM was explicitly scoped to ensemble membership only and stated that gru4rec_seq standalone quality remained a separate open question.

code_summary: Train the existing best-known menu configuration once via the library, but inject capture_epoch_scores into the underlying config so we retain every epoch's validation score vector. Then evaluate held-out-user checkpoint selection rules with selection_rule_test/capture_selection_rule_test over those stored epoch predictions, writing the official single-run metrics required by the harness plus a sidecar diagnostic JSON. Existing menu primitives cannot express this because they choose how to train, not how to audit or compare model-selection rules on the same trained trajectory.
